question: When was the last time that Samuel saw Saul?
summary: 1 Samuel 15:35 states emphatically that "Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death." 1 Samuel 19:24 then has Saul stripping naked and prophesying before Samuel during the David-pursuit episode. The narrator first closes the door on Samuel/Saul contact, then opens it again four chapters later.

reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read 15:35 as Samuel ceasing to seek Saul out, not denying that Saul later came before him in 19:24.

discrepancy.connective: Henry Preserved Smith renders 15:35 "Samuel saw Saul no more till the day of his death" and holds that the plain sense flatly contradicts the encounter narrated in 19:24.

skeptic.name: Henry Preserved Smith
skeptic.work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Samuel (International Critical Commentary)
skeptic.attribution: Henry Preserved Smith (d. 1927), A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Samuel, ICC (1899)

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), at 1 Samuel 15:35
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke addresses this exact discrepancy on the passage: he grants that Saul went to Samuel at Naioth (19:22-24) but argues this does not affect 15:35, since from that time Samuel had no further connection with Saul as king.

link.note: No on-topic page found on an allowlisted domain for this specific tension; the nearest defendinginerrancy.com entry on 1 Samuel 19:23-24 treats a different question (the Spirit upon a rejected Saul), so link omitted rather than mismatched.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: not that he saw him no more, he saw him afterwards, Sa1 19:24, but it was accidentally, he did not go to see him, but Saul came to him …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the apparent conflict (15:35 vs 19:24) and resolves it on the mechanism the harmonizers all use: Samuel did not go to Saul; Saul came to Samuel. Strongest single reconcile, parity-capped at 1 to match the discrepancy pole's named-skeptic count.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death,.... Or "added not to see him" (x); not that he saw him no more, he saw him afterwards, Sa1 19:24, but it was accidentally, he did not go to see him, but Saul came to him; and Abarbinel supposes he might not see him then, but hid his face from him; and he observes that it is said:
until the day of his death; which intimates, he thinks, that he saw him after his death, when raised up by the witch of Endor; but that Samuel was then really raised, and was seen, wants proof. The meaning of the expression here is no more than this, that Samuel afterwards did not visit Saul as he used to do; he did not go to him, to give him his advice and counsel, as he wonted:
nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul; because of his sin, his impenitence, and hypocrisy; and because of the loss of the kingdom to him, and to his posterity; and he might be concerned also about his eternal welfare; for he appears to have a natural affection for him, and was far from envying him as his rival, and rejoicing at his fall:
and the Lord repented that he made Saul king over Israel; nor was his mind altered, neither by the hypocritical confession of Saul, nor by the cordial prayers and heart of Samuel; see Sa1 15:11.
(x) "et non addidit ad videndum", Montanus.
